Title: Strip ontosage:isSimulated from the building data
Why: D1: all data is the building's data. Provenance is disclosed once in the paper (680 physical sensors, the rest modelled on them), not hedged in every answer.
Approach: A re-runnable script that removes the property and rewrites the file; not hand-edited, so it can be applied or inverted per building.
Building_agnostic: Operates on whatever TTL the active building ships; names no building.
Acceptance: grep -r isSimulated returns nothing under the active building's TTL; every file still parses; triple count drops by the expected 4,135.
Notes: Recoverable from git history if ever needed.

Title: Remove the property and its provenance text from the schema
Why: A property nothing writes and nothing reads is a trap for the next reader.
Evidence: ontology/ontosage_schema.ttl line 868 and the Module F note at 1091
Approach: Delete the declaration and the paragraph that explains the real/simulated split.
Building_agnostic: Schema is shared by every building.
Acceptance: Schema parses; no ontosage:isSimulated remains; the conformance suite still passes.

Title: Remove the code paths that read the flag
Why: With one kind of data, any branch on provenance is dead weight that can still change an answer.
Approach: Delete the branches; keep the behaviour of the TRUE side (treat every record as a real record).
Building_agnostic: No building literals involved.
Acceptance: No module reads the flag; unit suite green in the parked state.

Title: Stop ranking records by provenance
Why: The deliberation lane can prefer a measured record over a modelled one. Left in, every ranking silently biases toward the 680 physical sensors while the system claims all data is equal. This is the subtlest part of D1.
Approach: Remove the provenance term from the score; keep coverage and freshness terms.
Building_agnostic: Scoring is over whatever sensors the building has.
Acceptance: A ranking over a mixed set puts a modelled sensor first when its reading is better; a test pins it.

Title: Retire the placeholder vocabulary from stored prose
Why: The flag is already stripped from answers (BUG-699), so the real leak is wording: 'Defibrillators are modelled at reception', 'to be replaced by real data'.
Evidence: Pack index #71 (AED); 45 TTL files carry placeholder phrasing
Approach: Rewrite locationText/answerText so a record states a fact or is absent.
Building_agnostic: Wording lives in per-building TTL.
Acceptance: No shipped answer contains 'modelled', 'placeholder' or 'to be replaced'; a test scans the TTL for the vocabulary.

Title: PROTECT_ENFORCE=off and remove the access-policy preamble
Why: D2: one role for now. It also removes 'Served at 5-second resolution - this building's access policy sets the finest detail available to you', which opens many answers in the pack, and takes the PDP out of every data turn.
Evidence: Pack indexes 16, 38, 60, 70 open with the preamble; PDP consulted on every data turn
Approach: One setting, plus deleting the wording it drives.
Building_agnostic: One setting; the policy engine stays in the tree for reinstatement.
Acceptance: No answer mentions an access policy or a clamped resolution; the same question answers identically from CLI and browser.
Notes: Does NOT disable the refusal to answer about a named individual - that lives outside the PDP and stays.

Title: Repoint owner_facts_report at absence only
Why: Its HEDGED/PLACEHOLDER states are defined by the flag that is going away.
Approach: Report one thing: safety-critical facts the building has not stated at all.
Building_agnostic: Reads config/safety_critical_facts.yaml against the active graph.
Acceptance: The checklist lists only genuinely absent facts.

Title: Confirm the three defibrillator positions (NEEDS THE OWNER)
Why: Closes BUG-858 (P1) as a data fix rather than a flag. Under D1 the system will state these positions as fact, and it is the one fact where a wrong value could hurt someone in an emergency.
Approach: Owner eyeballs reception / floor 3 / floor 5, then the word 'modelled' is removed.
Building_agnostic: Per-building safety data.
Acceptance: The record states three confirmed positions; BUG-858 closed.
Notes: The only item in Wave 0 that is not mine to do.

Title: Regression gate over the 73 questions already evidenced
Why: The pack is the promise. Every later wave must not break a question that already answers.
Approach: A harness that re-asks the 52 GOOD questions and fails if one stops answering; run before every merge.
Building_agnostic: Reads the pack; the questions are data, not code.
Acceptance: All 52 still answer after each wave; a deliberate improvement to a WEAK one is recorded, not silently accepted.
Notes: Baseline 51/51 behave as recorded. Its first full run found a verdict in the pack that described a different run's answer (#69) and a non-breaking hyphen that made a stable question look regressed. Lessons #130, #131.

Title: Route a question naming two measurands to a lane that reads both
Why: The single largest cause of failure in the pack.
Evidence: Cross-modal diagnosis 0/5 (pack 25, 27, 28, 29 and the delta-T question)
Approach: Concept stage: when two distinct measurand concepts resolve and it is not a register question, route to the multi-read lane.
Building_agnostic: The rule counts resolved concepts; it names none.
Acceptance: The five diagnosis questions reach the multi-read lane; the pinned precedence test is updated in the same commit.

Title: Fetch N modalities over one window per candidate space
Why: Nothing outside the deliberation lane can read two quantities at once.
Evidence: deliberation/fetch.py already does this for ranking; pack #14 proves it works
Approach: Generalise the fetch so any lane can request a list of modalities across a candidate set.
Building_agnostic: Modalities resolve from HBCO; storage routes by ref:storedAt.
Acceptance: A lane can ask for [co2, temperature, occupancy] and receive per-room series for each.

Title: Say what two series together mean, as recipes
Why: 'Warm and stuffy' and 'ventilation keeping up with occupancy' are judgements over two series. In code they would be building-specific; as recipes they are data.
Evidence: Pack 27, 28 return a decline or a false claim about what the model holds
Approach: Threshold/trend combinations expressed in config/recipes.yaml with a per-building overlay.
Building_agnostic: A new building adds a recipe row; no code change. This is the TTL-first contract applied to reasoning.
Acceptance: Both questions answer naming both quantities and the band each was judged against.

Title: Two windows, one answer
Why: Comparing two periods is never attempted: the second window is not fetched.
Evidence: Pack 22, 23 (this week vs last week; weekend vs weekday) - 0/3 period comparisons
Approach: Resolve both intervals through requested_interval, fetch both, compare, and state both windows in the answer.
Building_agnostic: Windows come from the parser in the building's local time; the store stays UTC.
Acceptance: Both questions answer with both periods' figures and the difference.

Title: Negation over the model
Why: 'Which rooms have NO temperature sensor' is a set difference the graph can answer directly.
Approach: One SPARQL: spaces minus spaces that have a sensor of the class.
Building_agnostic: Pure Brick classes; no building literals.
Acceptance: The question returns the rooms, with a count and the class it tested.

Title: Route floor-level and building-level forecasts to the forecaster
Why: Per-room prediction works end to end; anything wider returns a register decline.
Approach: Extend the forecast trigger so a floor or building scope reaches the forecast agent.
Building_agnostic: Scope resolves from the graph's floors; no names.
Acceptance: Questions 2, 3 and 5 of the 50-set return a forecast with its model table.

Title: Aggregate first, then forecast
Why: A floor forecast must be over the floor's mean per bucket, not one sensor.
Evidence: aggregate_lane already computes per-bucket means with correct units and bands
Approach: Aggregate to an hourly series, then hand it to the existing forecasting pipeline.
Building_agnostic: Aggregation is over whatever sensors the floor has.
Acceptance: The forecast states the denominator: averaged over N sensors.

Title: Cross-entity prediction with honest overlap
Why: 'Will floor 3 be warmer than floor 4 tomorrow' needs two forecasts and an interval comparison.
Evidence: Asked for by the supervisor-facing plan; no pack question covers it yet
Approach: Forecast both, compare the confidence intervals, and say when they overlap instead of asserting a winner.
Building_agnostic: Entities come from the graph.
Acceptance: The answer names both forecasts and declines to pick a winner when the intervals overlap.

Title: Outdoor weather
Why: Weather and weather-correlation questions decline today.
Evidence: CAVEAT-844; pack #26 answers only the outside-air half
Approach: A weather feed plus <id>_weather.ttl. A real feed if one is available - ASKED, NO ANSWER YET.
Building_agnostic: feeds.yaml is per building; the adapter is generic.
Acceptance: 'How does today compare with the outside temperature' answers with both series.
Notes: Needs a yes/no on whether a campus weather API exists.

Title: One calibration register, one lane
Why: The same fact answered in one pack and denied in the other.
Evidence: Pack #40 answers 237 overdue; pack #49 says no calibration field exists
Approach: Single register; the lane that reads it is pinned by a test.
Building_agnostic: Register is per building; the lane is generic.
Acceptance: Both phrasings answer from the same register with the same number.

Title: Parking tariff, or a recorded absence
Why: The cost register holds 24 lines and no parking line, so the question declines.
Approach: Add the tariff if the building has one; otherwise leave absent so the decline stays honest.
Building_agnostic: Cost register is per building.
Acceptance: The question answers, or declines naming the register it looked in.

Title: Design occupancy per space
Why: Enables 'observed against design' comparisons, a strong viva question.
Evidence: No pack question answers it today
Approach: ontosage:designOccupancy on spaces.
Building_agnostic: A property on whatever spaces the building declares.
Acceptance: 'How does observed occupancy compare with design' answers with both numbers.

Title: Last-seen timestamp per sensor, derived
Why: 'Which sensors stopped reporting and when' is answered vaguely.
Approach: Derive from the store, never author it; a sensor's silence is a fact about the data.
Building_agnostic: Derived from whatever stores the building registers.
Acceptance: The question names the silent sensors and the time each was last seen.

Title: A provenance intent over the previous turn
Why: Every answer carries an evidence record; the system cannot say it.
Approach: Read the previous turn's evidence record from turn_memory and render it.
Building_agnostic: The record is built per turn from whatever sources answered.
Acceptance: 'Which data sources did you use' names the sources of the previous answer.

Title: Publish the precedence rules as records
Why: 'If two records disagree, which wins' is answered from prose today, or not at all.
Approach: Express precedence as a record class the metadata lane reads.
Building_agnostic: Rules are about record classes, not buildings.
Acceptance: The question answers from the graph.

Title: Rolling session summary that survives the turn ceiling
Why: Today the window is hard: 20 verbatim turns plus 30 one-line summaries. Turn 51 silently loses the earliest history, and the one-liners are deterministic extracts, not a narrative of what the user is doing.
Approach: Compact turns beyond the window into a rolling summary that is updated as the session grows, so history is compressed rather than dropped.
Building_agnostic: Summarises whatever was asked; no building vocabulary.
Acceptance: A 60-turn conversation still answers a question about turn 3.

Title: Carry the summary on every entry point
Why: Long-term context is injected on /v1/chat/completions only; /chat and the websocket do not get it.
Approach: One helper that builds the context block, called by every chat entry point.
Building_agnostic: Generic.
Acceptance: The same follow-up works through /chat, /v1 and the websocket.

Title: Cross-session memory for a returning user
Why: A new chat starts blank. Other assistants recall what a user cares about.
Evidence: A user_memory Qdrant collection exists and is not used for this
Approach: Per-user preferences and recurring subjects, recalled at session start, always visible to the user and clearable.
Building_agnostic: Per user, not per building.
Acceptance: A returning user's stated preference is honoured in a new session, and can be listed and deleted.
Notes: Personal data: the user must be able to see and erase it.

Title: Prove the memory with a long-conversation test
Why: A memory feature without a long test is a memory feature that works only in demos.
Approach: A 60-turn scripted conversation asserting recall at turns 3, 25 and 59.
Building_agnostic: Generic.
Acceptance: Recall holds at all three points; the injected context stays within the model's window.

Title: Make routing deterministic for a fixed question
Why: Six of fifty answers differed between two identical runs. Until this closes, no single-run pass rate is trustworthy to better than about ten points - including the 52/73.
Approach: Cache the classifier decision per normalised question, as the concept match already does; make the tie-breaks explicit.
Building_agnostic: Cache key is the question, not the building.
Acceptance: The same question asked five times takes the same lane five times.

Title: Latency
Why: Median 100 s, slowest 273 s. Acceptable for a demonstration, not for use.
Approach: Profile the register and metadata lanes first; forecasts are genuinely expensive and stay slow.
Building_agnostic: Generic.
Acceptance: Median under 30 s for non-forecast questions.

Title: Draw and label a fresh held-out set
Why: Sets C-L are spent. A rate measured on questions the system was tuned on is not a rate.
Approach: Seeded draw, hand-labelled, published with its denominator.
Building_agnostic: Drawn from the question bank, not from a building.
Acceptance: A rate with its denominator and its date, on questions nobody tuned against.

Title: Re-run the 73-question pack and re-read every answer
Why: The pass rate is a property of a build, not of the project.
Approach: Re-capture, re-read, re-publish the pack with the new numbers.
Building_agnostic: Generic.
Acceptance: A new pack with its own date and verdicts; the README's numbers match it.
